title: Cross-domain lookup and reasoning skills
goal: Compare extractive accuracy across unrelated domains and record which reasoning skills the non-generative engine actually performs.
method: Six domains have four original passages each. Comparison, counting, ordering, and sums run in code on extracted values. The conditional probe is a single if/unless sentence.
results_prose: Per-domain accuracy on 4 items each: {'software': 0.75, 'recipes': 0.25, 'sports': 0.75, 'finance': 0.75, 'medical': 0.75, 'legal': 1.0}. The gap between the highest and lowest domain is 0.75. Skills that succeeded: ['comparison', 'counting', 'ordering', 'sum', 'conditional_if']. Skills that failed: ['conditional_unless_blocked']. The conditional helper returns the 'if' result and does not block on 'unless', so the unless probe fails on purpose.
conclusion: Domain differences on this set come from wording, not from pretrained domain knowledge, because no pretrained model is loaded. The engine does comparison, counting, ordering, sum, conditional_if and fails conditional_unless_blocked.
scale_down: Four items in each of six domains replace 20 items in five domains. Ordering uses dateparser rather than a learned temporal model.
